title: Bernoulli restriction of a narrow DNF to a narrow CNF, with high probability
statement:
Let $g$ be a DNF formula on $n \ge 1$ variables whose width is at most $w$, where $w \ge 1$, and suppose that within each term of $g$ any two literals having the same variable are equal and no literal is repeated. Let $l$ be a natural number, and let $p$ be a real number with $0 < p \le 1$ and $p \le \tfrac{1}{40w}$. Then, under a Bernoulli$(p)$ random restriction $\rho$, the probability that the restricted function $g|_\rho$ is computed by no CNF formula of width at most $l$ is at most
\[
  \left(\tfrac{1}{2}\right)^{l} + \exp\!\left(-\tfrac{np}{3}\right).
\]

replaced:
Let $g$ be a $\mathrm{DNF}$ of width at most $w>0$ (with distinct variables per term and
no duplicate literals), let $n>0$, and let $0<p\le \tfrac{1}{40w}$ with $p\le 1$. Then the
probability under a Bernoulli$(p)$ restriction $\rho$ that $g|_\rho$ cannot be expressed as a
$\mathrm{CNF}$ of width at most $l$ is at most
\[
  \Bigl(\tfrac12\Bigr)^l + \exp\!\Bigl(-\tfrac{np}{3}\Bigr).
\]
